chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Sayyar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A grave robber was seized in the era of Muawiya, so he said to his companions, 'What are your views?' So they said, 'Punish him and free his way'. So a man from the people said, 'This is not what Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) did'. He (Muawiya) said, 'So what did he do?' So he said, 'He cut (the hand) of the grave robber and said, 'He is a thief, and a desecrator of the dead'.

key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةَ: Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan, Umayyad Caliph
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: He is cut (referring to amputation of the hand)

ai.seo_question: What was the legal ruling of Imam Ali regarding grave robbers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential precedent that grave robbers are treated as thieves (sariq) subject to the hadd of hand amputation, a ruling attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) and applied during Muawiya's era. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the desecration of the dead constitutes a property crime against the deceased, thereby justifying the standard theft penalty rather than a discretionary punishment.
